To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the homotopy pullback of bicategories can be defined by a certain bicategorical homotopy-fibred product, that it exists under certain conditions, and that it can be described in a way that allows us to apply it in the study of crossed modules and of the homotopical theory of monoidal categories.
the homotopy pullback of two functors $A\to B\leftarrow A'$ is equivalent, under certain conditions, to the bicategory of spans between the bicategories $A$ and $A'$.
the homotopy pullback of the classifying spaces of a diagram of bicategory is the classifying space of the homotopical pullback of the diagram.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the homotopical properties of the homotopic pullback in the bicategorical setting.
the study of homology and homotopy theories in the bicategorical context.
the homotopy-theoretical aspects of the theory of bicategories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for a diagram of bicategorical objects, the bicategory-theoretical homotopy pullback of the induced diagram of classifying spaces coincides with the homotopy pull-back in the usual sense of homotopy theory.

the homotopy type of the homotopical fibre product of two bicategories $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$ is given by the classifying space of the homotopic fibre product $\mathbf{Fib}_{\mathbf{Cat}}\left(\mathbf{A},\mathbf{B}\right)$ of the underlying categories, where the latter is a homotopical version of the usual categorical pullback.

the homotopy type of the homotopical pullback of the nerve of a diagram of bicategorical data is given by the homotopy pullback of the induced maps of classifying spaces, under the assumption that the diagram is homotopical in a suitable sense.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to prove that the homotopy pullback of the classifying space of a diagram of bicategorical structures is the classifying space for the homotopy fibre product of the corresponding diagrams of structures.
we have found a new way to study the homotopy type of the classifying spaces of higher categorical structures.

, in a bicategorical context, the classifying space of the homotopical pullback of a diagram of bicategorical spaces is the homotopically pullback of the classifying spaces of the diagram of bicategories.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bicategories are a useful tool to understand the homotopy theory underlying the homotopy type of the classifying space of a category.

, in the presence of certain conditions, the homotopy type of a bicategory can be recovered from the homotopy pullback of its classifying space along the maps induced by its underlying category, its bicategory of spans, its bicategory with invertible 2-cells and its bicategory of 1-cells.

bicategories can be seen as higher categorical analogues of topological spaces, and the homotopies among their continuous maps are the analogues of homotopies among the continuous maps of topological spaces.
